The item comprises a substrate having at least one main surface provided with an interference coating. This interference coating is designed as a multilayer optical coating and includes at least one layer A having a refractive index less than or equal to 1.65.

Layer A is formed by vacuum deposition assisted by an ion source. During this deposition process, at least one organosilicon compound A is used as a precursor or source material, thereby contributing to the formation of the low-refractive-index layer.

The interference coating further includes one of the following layer configurations. In a first configuration, the coating comprises a high-refractive-index layer B formed from a metal oxide and an organosilicon compound B. In a second configuration, the coating comprises a thin silicon oxide layer C arranged in direct contact with a metal oxide layer E.

In either configuration, the high-refractive-index layer B or the metal oxide layer E contains at least one metal oxide having a refractive index greater than or equal to 1.8. This combination of low- and high-refractive-index materials allows the interference coating to provide the desired optical interference properties on the substrate surface.
outputs.L4:
An article is provided that includes a substrate bearing a multilayer interference coating. The substrate may be any suitable transparent, translucent, or reflective base material, depending on the intended optical application. On at least one surface of the substrate, a coating system is formed by ion-assisted vacuum deposition. The deposited coating comprises a plurality of layers arranged to produce optical interference effects, with the layers being selected and positioned according to their refractive indices and their contact relationships with adjacent layers.

The multilayer coating may be formed from materials derived from organosilicon compounds, metal oxides, silicon oxide, or combinations of these materials. In particular, the coating includes layers having relatively low refractive indices and layers having relatively high refractive indices. These layers are arranged in a predetermined sequence so that selected low-index layers are in direct contact with selected high-index layers, thereby creating interfaces that influence the reflection, transmission, color, and other optical properties of the coated article.

The use of ion-assisted vacuum deposition allows the coating layers to be formed with improved density, adhesion, and uniformity. This deposition technique can also enhance durability and environmental resistance while maintaining precise control over layer thickness and composition. Because the optical behavior of the coating depends on the interaction of light with the multiple interfaces between layers, careful selection of the refractive indices and layer order enables the coating to be tailored for specific performance requirements.

As a result, the coated substrate can exhibit controlled optical interference, such as reduced reflection, enhanced reflection, selective wavelength transmission, color control, or other desired optical effects. The described coating architecture therefore provides an improved multilayer interference coating suitable for use in optical components, display elements, architectural or automotive glazing, lenses, mirrors, filters, and other coated substrates requiring enhanced optical performance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a patent claim for an optical item having an interference coating with low-index and high-index layers deposited by ion-assisted vacuum deposition using organosilicon compounds and metal oxides.
counterfactuals.output:
The patent claim describes an optical item (such as an ophthalmic lens) with an interference coating made of alternating low-refractive-index and high-refractive-index layers. The coating is deposited by ion-assisted vacuum deposition.

The low-index layer is formed from organosilicon compounds, typically producing a silica-based material such as SiO₂ with improved density or adhesion. The high-index layer is formed from one or more metal oxides, such as titanium oxide, zirconium oxide, tantalum oxide, or similar high-index materials.

Together, these stacked layers create an optical interference effect, for example antireflection or reflective control, while the ion-assisted deposition process improves coating properties such as compactness, durability, adhesion, and environmental resistance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise patent-style description of an item comprising a substrate coated with an interference coating, including layer A with n ≤ 1.65, layer B with n > 1.65, and an optional thin silicon oxide layer C contacting a high-index metal oxide layer E.
counterfactuals.output: An article comprises a substrate bearing an interference coating. The interference coating includes at least one low-index layer A having a refractive index n ≤ 1.65 and at least one high-index layer B having a refractive index n > 1.65. In some embodiments, the coating further comprises a high-index metal oxide layer E and a silicon oxide layer C disposed in direct contact with the layer E. The silicon oxide layer C is a thin layer, preferably having a physical thickness selected to modify adhesion, durability, optical performance, or interfacial stability without substantially increasing the overall optical thickness of the coating. The layers may be arranged on the substrate in an order selected to provide a desired interference effect, including reflection reduction, color control, or spectral selectivity.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract-style summary of an invention involving an optical article with an interference coating made of organosilicon and metal oxide layers, specifying refractive index thresholds and direct contact relationships between the layers.
counterfactuals.output:
An optical article includes a transparent substrate bearing an interference coating configured to modify reflected and/or transmitted light. The interference coating comprises a multilayer stack including at least one organosilicon layer and at least one metal oxide layer. The organosilicon layer has a refractive index below a selected low-index threshold, for example less than or equal to 1.55 at 550 nm, and may comprise a silicon-based organic or hybrid material such as a siloxane, silsesquioxane, or plasma-deposited organosilicon compound. The metal oxide layer has a refractive index above a selected high-index threshold, for example greater than or equal to 1.60, preferably greater than or equal to 1.80, at 550 nm, and may comprise titanium oxide, zirconium oxide, tantalum oxide, niobium oxide, hafnium oxide, tin oxide, aluminum oxide, or mixtures thereof.

The organosilicon and metal oxide layers are arranged to form an optical interference structure, such as an antireflective, reflective, filtering, or color-control coating. In certain embodiments, the organosilicon layer is in direct physical contact with the metal oxide layer, without an intervening adhesion, primer, or barrier layer. In other embodiments, the coating includes a sequence in which a first metal oxide layer directly contacts a first organosilicon layer, and the first organosilicon layer directly contacts a second metal oxide layer, thereby forming adjacent high-index/low-index interfaces. The direct contact relationships provide controlled optical phase contrast while maintaining coating compactness and adhesion. The optical article may be an ophthalmic lens, display cover, optical filter, visor, window, or transparent protective element.
